plan.exit_criteria: both algorithms negotiate; monitoring shows which peers use which
plan.rollback: switch AES-256 off again — 3DES never stopped working
plan.title: Wave 1: enable AES-256 next to 3DES

actions: Payment HSM: prefer AES-256; move each connected peer and vendor once it confirms
plan.exit_criteria: handshakes, signatures and business transactions succeed on the new algorithm for every listed system
plan.providers_first: systems that others call move before their callers
plan.title: Wave 1: move to AES-256

actions: re-scan the changed systems so the twin shows the new algorithm
run each business process's smoke test
confirm no connection still negotiates 3DES
plan.exit_criteria: the twin no longer reports 3DES on these systems
plan.title: Verify on the twin and in production

actions: disable 3DES once every peer and vendor has confirmed AES-256
keep 3DES keys read-only until stored data is re-encrypted
plan.exit_criteria: no system, peer or vendor depends on 3DES
plan.rollback: re-enable 3DES (keys are destroyed only after a holding period)
plan.title: Retire 3DES

ripple.effect: directly connected to a system that changes — its connection must accept AES-256 or keep 3DES
ripple.name: SWIFT Gateway

ripple.effect: 2 hops away: not changed itself, but it depends on a chain that does — an outage on the way reaches it
ripple.name: Core Banking

ripple.effect: 3 hops away: not changed itself, but it depends on a chain that does — an outage on the way reaches it
ripple.name: Branch Banking

strategy.direct_is_safe_when: no connected system outside the change, no network endpoint with unseen clients, no vendor, no stored data or signatures under the old algorithm, and every device's capability is recorded
strategy.meaning: run the old and the new algorithm side by side, then retire the old one

parallel_mechanisms.how: write new data under AES-256, keep 3DES keys read-only until the stored data is re-encrypted
make the algorithm a per-connection setting so each peer and vendor moves on its own date and can be rolled back alone

systems.name: Payment HSM
why_in_change: a twin crypto asset of this system uses it
source evidence linked to this system uses it

unknowns: 2 listed component(s) belong to no system through an evidenced edge, so no connection effect can be traced for them
VBOM capabilities and contracts are what vendors and the register declare — not observed on the estate
clients of a network endpoint are not assets in the twin, so they cannot be checked
hardware and vendor capability is as recorded or declared — not independently tested
performance of the new algorithm on this estate is not measured here
which algorithm each connection negotiates is not recorded on dependency edges; a connected system is treated as needing the old algorithm until it confirms
